target_customer: Independent and multi-unit restaurant operators wanting repeat guests
problem: Over 60% of a restaurant's customers never return for a second visit (launch post), and owners lack time to run text marketing and feedback.
business_model: Managed SaaS and service subscription for restaurants
product_category: Restaurant SMS marketing, reviews and loyalty automation

founders.name: Shane Murphy
prior_employers: Jolt (restaurant operations software, acquired by Digi)
previous_startups: Online ordering company acquired by StrideQ
founders.background_notes: YC page: ran sales at Jolt, early team and investor at American HealthCare Lending.

founders.name: Mikey Murphy
previous_startups: Techstars 2016 company, three stints as CTO (names not given)

competitors.name: Attentive
competitors.what: SMS marketing platform that integrated with restaurant loyalty vendor Punchh

competitors.name: Punchh
competitors.traction_then: Named as Attentive's restaurant loyalty integration partner in 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: SMS campaigns, review routing and POS data integration are standard SaaS; later a US patent was awarded for the marketing technology (company blog).

defensibility.rationale: Managed service and integrated guest lists create some stickiness, but SMS marketing tools were widely available.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; Boostly raised a $22M Series A in 2025.

market_need_then: The launch post cites over 60% of guests never returning and a February 2022 NRN report showed text subscribers visited 44% more often than non-subscribers.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful: 'Nobody deletes a text they can win', 'Marketing should be fun, not cringe'

branding.brand_signature: Gamified texts and physical Tap Cards
branding.community_and_virality: Customer spotlight posts and a restaurant podcast; no merch or fan evidence found

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct playful voice and a physical product asset, but little third party press about the brand itself.

pivots.from: Earlier products before YC (launch post says several pivots)
pivots.to: Text marketing and feedback for restaurants
pivots.why: Launch post says it reached about $1M annual revenue from outbound sales after several pivots; details not given

outcome_analysis: Boostly was bootstrapped from 2017, joined YC in Summer 2022 with about $1M in revenue, and raised a $5.6M seed in August 2024 followed by a $22M Series A in February 2025. It reports serving over 1,200 locations. Its path shows revenue-led growth in a crowded SMS category, with later capital rather than early capital.
notes: Seed and Series A are each stated by the press release plus a trade outlet. One source reports $1.7M raised after YC; unverified and not recorded. The 2022 competitor list is from an April 2022 Attentive blog, not Boostly's own materials; the YC page names no competitors. The 1,200 locations and 10x engagement figures are company claims.
